mean: to be unable to keep a secret
lit: one's mouth is light: words float out of it easily

use.how: Describes a person's habit, as a predicate: あの人は口が軽い. A warning or complaint, never praise for being chatty or friendly.

near.diff: 口が滑る is one accidental slip on one occasion; 口が軽い is a person's habit of passing secrets on.
口が堅い is the opposite: someone you can trust with a secret.

mean: to be good at keeping secrets

use.how: Describes someone you can trust with confidential matters: 彼女は口が堅い. Usually written 堅い; 固い is also seen.

near.diff: 口が軽い is the opposite: someone who passes secrets on.
頭が固い is rigid, inflexible thinking; 口が堅い is only about not revealing what one has been told.

cue: You need to tell someone about a personal problem and want to be sure it won't go any further. Why do you choose this particular colleague?

mean: to offer unwanted opinions on others' affairs
lit: to put one's mouth out into something that is not one's own

use.how: Takes に for the matter meddled in: 人の家のことに口を出す. Often in requests or complaints: 口を出さないで.

near.diff: 手を出す is getting involved in or trying something yourself; 口を出す is commenting on what others are doing.

mean: to have a sharp tongue, to speak harshly
lit: one's mouth is bad: what comes out of it is rough

use.how: Describes how someone habitually talks; often softened with けど: 口は悪いけど優しい. Used of a person, not of one remark.

near.diff: 口が軽い is leaking secrets; 口が悪い is saying things bluntly or rudely.

mean: to let something slip by accident

use.how: About one occasion, often with つい or うっかり: つい口が滑った. The transitive 口を滑らせる is also common.

near.diff: 口が軽い is a habit of leaking secrets; 口が滑る is one unintended slip, which can happen to anyone.

cue: In the middle of a chat you accidentally mention your friend's engagement, which was supposed to be secret, and you immediately regret it. What happened?

mean: to look over, to skim through a document

mean: so busy that any help at all would be welcome

near.diff: 目が回る only describes a frantic pace; 猫の手も借りたい adds that you would welcome help from anyone.
手が離せない means you can't break off from what you're doing right now; it says nothing about wanting help.

cue: It's harvest time, the farm is short of workers, and the farmer says even the family pet would be useful right now. What expression fits?

ctx.s: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの準備[じゅんび]で{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}ほど忙[いそが]しく、小[ちい]さい子供[こども]たちにも手伝[てつだ]わせた。
ctx.en: Getting ready to move kept us so busy that we'd take help from anyone, so we even had the little ones pitch in.

ctx.s: 「手伝[てつだ]おうか？」「ありがとう！今[いま]は{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}くらいなんだ。」
ctx.en: "Want a hand?" "Thanks! Right now I'd be grateful for any help at all."

ctx.s: 収穫[しゅうかく]の時期[じき]、農家[のうか]は{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}ほどの忙[いそが]しさだ。
ctx.en: At harvest time farmers are so busy that every pair of hands counts.

ctx.s: 年末[ねんまつ]の郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]は{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}状態[じょうたい]で、学生[がくせい]のアルバイトを大勢[おおぜい]雇[やと]う。
ctx.en: At the end of the year the post office is desperate for help and hires lots of students part-time.

ctx.s: 人手[ひとで]が足[た]りない店[みせ]で、店長[てんちょう]は「{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}よ」とこぼしていた。
ctx.en: At the understaffed shop, the manager grumbled that he'd take help from the cat if he could.

ctx.s: 結婚式[けっこんしき]の前日[ぜんじつ]は{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}ほどで、友人[ゆうじん]たちが飾[かざ]り付[つ]けを手伝[てつだ]ってくれた。
ctx.en: The day before the wedding was so hectic that we needed all the help we could get, and friends pitched in with the decorations.

bad.s: 部長[ぶちょう]、{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}ので、ぜひ手伝[てつだ]ってください。
bad.en: (meant: Sir, I'm swamped, so please help me)
bad.why: Said to a specific person, it compares their help to a cat's paw, which is rude, especially to a superior.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は親切[しんせつ]で、いつも{猫[ねこ]の手[て]も借[か]りたい}人[ひと]だ。
bad.en: (meant: he is kind and always willing to help)
bad.why: It describes being swamped and needing help, not being a helpful person.
